summary.text: For the index $n=9$, the primorial is $2\cdot3\cdot5\cdot7\cdot11\cdot13\cdot17\cdot19\cdot23=223092870$, and the resulting term satisfies $49770428644836901=29^2\cdot59180057841661$. Since $29$ is prime, this term is not squarefree, so the asserted conjunction already fails independently of its infinitude clause.

full_proof.text:
Let
\[
P_n=\prod_{k=0}^{n-1}p_k,
\]
where \(p_0=2,p_1=3,p_2=5,\ldots\) are the primes in increasing order. Thus the sequence in question is
\[
a(n)=P_n^2+1.
\]
We disprove the assertion that every term is squarefree by considering \(n=9\).

The first nine primes are
\[
2,3,5,7,11,13,17,19,23.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\begin{aligned}
P_9
 &=2\cdot3\cdot5\cdot7\cdot11\cdot13\cdot17\cdot19\cdot23\\
 &=223092870.
\end{aligned}
\]
For completeness, the successive products are
\[
2,\ 6,\ 30,\ 210,\ 2310,\ 30030,\ 510510,\ 9699690,\ 223092870,
\]
which confirms this value of the ninth primorial.

We will show that the square of the prime \(29\) divides \(a(9)\). First, \(29\) is prime: if it were composite, it would have a prime divisor at most \(\sqrt{29}<6\), hence one of \(2,3,5\). It is divisible by none of these, so it is prime.

Now \(29^2=841\), and direct division of the primorial gives
\[
223092870=841\cdot265270+800.
\]
Thus
\[
P_9\equiv 800\pmod{841}.
\]
The crucial residue calculation is
\[
800^2+1=640001=841\cdot761.
\]
It follows that
\[
P_9^2+1\equiv800^2+1\equiv0\pmod{841}.
\]
Therefore
\[
29^2=841\mid a(9).
\]
One can also see the divisibility directly by writing \(q=265270\). Since \(P_9=841q+800\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
a(9)
  &=(841q+800)^2+1\\
  &=841^2q^2+2\cdot841\cdot800q+(800^2+1)\\
  &=841\bigl(841q^2+1600q+761\bigr).
\end{aligned}
\]
Numerically, the term and its exact factorization by \(29^2\) are
\[
a(9)=223092870^2+1=49770428644836901
     =841\cdot59180057841661.
\]

A positive integer is squarefree precisely when the square of no prime divides it. Since \(29\) is prime and \(29^2\mid a(9)\), the number \(a(9)\) is not squarefree. Hence the universal assertion
\[
\forall n\ge 0,\quad a(n)\text{ is squarefree}
\]
is false.

The proposed combined conjecture is the conjunction of this universal squarefreeness assertion with the assertion that \(a(n)\) is prime for infinitely many indices \(n\). A conjunction cannot hold when one of its components is false. Therefore
\[
\neg\left(\bigl(\forall n,\ a(n)\text{ is squarefree}\bigr)
\land
\bigl(\text{there are infinitely many }n\text{ for which }a(n)\text{ is prime}\bigr)\right).
\]
Thus \(n=9\), via the repeated prime factor \(29^2\), is a counterexample to the squarefreeness clause and disproves the stated combined conjecture. This argument makes no claim about whether infinitely many terms of the sequence are prime; that separate question is unnecessary for the disproof of the conjunction.
